Quantify the home range using autocorrelated kernel density estimation

Source: R/hr_tt_akde.R
hr_tt_akde.Rd

This function estimates the home range of each track using autocorrelated kernel density estimation (AKDE, Fleming et al. 2015), as implemented in the package ctmm (ctmm::akde()). Unlike conventional kernel density estimation (hr_tt_kde()), AKDE accounts for the autocorrelation of locations in tracking data, which otherwise leads to underestimating home ranges. AKDE requires a movement model for each track, which must first be fitted with ctmm_tt_fit().

Usage

hr_tt_akde(
  x,
  models,
  bbox = NULL,
  res = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  weights = FALSE,
  debias = TRUE,
  tolerance = 0.001,
  ci_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

x

A move2 object, in a projected coordinate reference system with units in metres (the same used to fit the models). If grouped, each group must contain a single track; otherwise, the track id is used as grouping variable.

models

A table of movement models created with ctmm_tt_fit() (with a model for each track in x).

bbox

A named vector of four elements (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) defining a grid shared by all groups, or a list of one such vector per group. If NULL (the default), a shared grid that contains all the UDs is created (see Details).

res

The resolution of the grid (in metres). Supply one value for a shared resolution or one value per group. If NULL (the default), the resolution follows the default of ctmm (see Details); with a list of bbox (one per group), each group has its own default resolution.

Per-group values of bbox and res are matched to the groups in the order of dplyr::group_keys() (i.e. sorted by the grouping variables).

levels

A vector of levels for the isopleths (i.e. contour lines), as numbers between 0 and 1. If NULL (the default), the full UD is returned; otherwise just the isopleths are returned (see hr_tt_kde()).

weights

Logical; if TRUE, the locations are weighted to account for irregular sampling and gaps in the tracks (Fleming et al. 2018). This is recommended for irregularly sampled tracks, but it is slower. Default is FALSE.

debias

Logical; whether to correct the bias of the estimate of the home range area (see ctmm::akde()). Default is TRUE.

tolerance

The target error of the numerical computations of ctmm::akde() (its error argument), which also defines the default grid (the probability mass of each UD outside the grid). A warning is given if more than this (and more than 1%) of a UD is outside the grid (e.g. with a bbox that is too small). Default is 0.001.

ci_level

The confidence level of the confidence intervals of the home range areas, returned when levels is set. Default is 0.95.

Value

Either a tibble of class hr_tt_ud_tbl, or, if levels is not NULL, an sf tibble of class hr_tt_poly_tbl (as returned by hr_tt_ud_iso()), with columns:

  • the grouping variable (as named in x; if x is grouped by multiple variables, this column is named group_id): the ids from the grouping of x

  • method: the method used to estimate the home range ("akde")

  • model_name: the name of the movement model used

  • dof_area: the effective number of degrees of freedom of the home range area (small values imply very uncertain estimates)

  • xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax: the bounding box of the grid

  • res: the resolution of the grid If levels is NULL:

  • ud: the UDs, as a list-column of terra::SpatRaster objects

  • ud_ctmm: the UDs, as a list-column of ctmm UD objects Else, if levels is not NULL, there is one row per group and level, and the following columns are added:

  • level: the level of the isopleth

  • area: the area of the isopleth (computed from its polygon)

  • area_low, area_high: the confidence interval of the home range area at this level, as estimated by ctmm (its point estimate, computed from the UD rather than from the polygon, can differ slightly from area)

  • geometry: an sfc column containing the multipolygons representing the isopleth for the appropriate level

Details

The utilisation distributions (UDs) are estimated on a grid shared by all groups (unless a bbox is given for each group), so that they can be combined or compared (e.g. with hr_tt_ud_sum() or hr_tt_ud_overlap()). By default, the grid follows the defaults of ctmm::akde(): its resolution is a tenth of the smallest bandwidth (or of the smallest standard deviation of the home range of the movement model) among all groups, and it extends far enough from the locations to contain all but a fraction tolerance of each UD. The cells are square, so that the grid can be used with the other hr_tt_ functions.

Each UD is estimated by ctmm directly on the grid (i.e. it is not resampled), and is standardised to sum to 1 over the grid. The ctmm UD objects are also returned (in column ud_ctmm), so that they can be used with other functions of ctmm (e.g. ctmm::overlap() or ctmm::meta()), and so that hr_tt_ud_iso() can compute the confidence intervals of the areas of the isopleths of the UDs (i.e. hr_tt_ud_iso(hr_tt_akde(x, models), levels) returns the same isopleths as hr_tt_akde(x, models, levels = levels), without estimating the UDs again).

The models are matched to the tracks by track id. As models are fitted to each track, each group of x must contain a single track (which is the case when x is not grouped). The tracks must not have changed since the models were fitted (i.e. they must have the same events with a location). Models without a home range (e.g. Brownian motion) cannot be used.

References

Fleming, C.H., Fagan, W.F., Mueller, T., Olson, K.A., Leimgruber, P. & Calabrese, J.M. (2015) Rigorous home range estimation with movement data: a new autocorrelated kernel density estimator. Ecology, 96, 1182-1188.

Fleming, C.H., Sheldon, D., Fagan, W.F., Leimgruber, P., Mueller, T., Nandintsetseg, D., Noonan, M.J., Olson, K.A., Setyawan, E., Sianipar, A. & Calabrese, J.M. (2018) Correcting for missing and irregular data in home-range estimation. Ecological Applications, 28, 1003-1010.

See also

ctmm_tt_fit() to fit the movement models, hr_tt_akde_pop() to combine the UDs into population UDs, hr_tt_kde() for conventional kernel density estimation.

Examples

data(buffalo, package = "ctmm")
buffalo_tt <- mt_as_move2(buffalo)
# we use a subset of the first two buffalo to make the example fast
buffalo_sub <- buffalo_tt %>%
  filter_by_meta(track %in% c("Cilla", "Gabs")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(track) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 100) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()
buffalo_fit <- ctmm_tt_fit(buffalo_sub, model = "ou")
#> Minimum sampling interval of 59 minutes in Cilla
#> Minimum sampling interval of 57 minutes in Gabs
buffalo_akde <- hr_tt_akde(buffalo_sub, buffalo_fit)
buffalo_akde
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   track method model_name     dof_area   xmin    ymin   xmax   ymax   res
#>   <chr> <chr>  <chr>             <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 Cilla akde   OU anisotropic     3.29 22253. -12568. 55239. 14083.  218.
#> 2 Gabs  akde   OU anisotropic     1.68 22253. -12568. 55239. 14083.  218.
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: ud <named list>, ud_ctmm <named list>
library(ggplot2)
autoplot(buffalo_akde)

# the 50% and 95% isopleths, with confidence intervals on their area
hr_tt_akde(buffalo_sub, buffalo_fit, levels = c(0.5, 0.95))
